most_likely_explanation: Ephemeris-match false positive. The 10.79-d, ~800-ppm dip is the 12.5%-deep primary eclipse of the Kp 10.14 detached eclipsing binary KIC 11285625 = KOI-7431.01 (Kepler EB catalogue P = 10.790444 +- 0.000032 d, BJD0 = 142.33451 BKJD; KOI catalogued at P/2 = 5.395256 d with koi_fpflag_ss = 1), 5.63 arcmin away on the same CCD channel in all four seasons (ch 79/51/7/35). Our period matches to dP/P = 2.6e-5 (re-derivation) / 5.3e-5 (pipeline) and our t0 falls within 0.6 h of the EB primary minimum. The eclipse is imprinted additively (~1.5-3 e/s) on KBONUS PSF light curves channel-wide by the KBONUS extraction: it appears at the EB ephemeris in the KBONUS flux of the Kp 13.6 TPF host KIC 11285496 (65 +- 16 ppm, 4.2 sigma, 2.7 e/s) and of pool star kic-011285117 (582 +- 94 ppm, 6.2 sigma, 2.0 e/s), but is absent from the official Kepler SAP/PDCSAP of KIC 11285496 (-14 +- 13 / -7 +- 10 ppm) and from the target's own raw pixels in the season where the KBONUS dip is strongest (-0.06 +- 0.45 e/s vs 1.8 e/s expected). The dip amplitude depends on the CCD (391 / 825 / 1634 ppm in seasons 3 / 0 / 1; 3.9 sigma between seasons), and the pipeline's 160-ppm 'secondary' is the EB's residual secondary eclipse (ratio ~0.15-0.37, same in all contaminated sources). The pipeline missed it because the ephemeris match is confined to a 3-arcmin cone.
kill_reasons: Period and epoch match with KIC 11285625 / KOI-7431.01 (Kp 10.14, 104,242-ppm eclipse, FALSE POSITIVE with significant-secondary flag): Kirk+2016 EB period 10.790444 +- 0.000032 d vs ours 10.790158 (re-derivation, dP/P = -2.6e-5) / 10.791014 (pipeline, +5.3e-5); EB primary BJD0 = 142.33451 BKJD vs our t0 131.52143 (pipeline, -0.5 h) and 843.73888 (re-derivation, +0.6 h). Chance probability of such a match among the ~22 TCEs within 12 arcmin is ~1e-5.

Same CCD channel every season: our TPF (KIC 11285496) and the EB's TPF are both on ch 79 (s0), 51 (s1), 7 (s2), 35 (s3); EB at CCD col ~722-726, row ~918-922 vs target col 639-643, row 938-943 (headers in redteam/geometry.log, eb_tpf.log).

The EB's own eclipse profile (official SAP of KIC 11285625, primary 0.1251, secondary 0.0869, 6.8 h wide, rounded V) fits the target's PSF flux at 952 +- 136 ppm (SNR 7.0) and reproduces the pipeline/re-derivation 'secondary' (247 ppm, 2.6 sigma) as the EB's residual secondary; the same suppressed secondary (ratio ~0.15) appears in the other contaminated sources.

Depth depends on the CCD, not the star: template amplitude 825 / 1634 / 391 ppm on ch 79 / 51 / 35; T14-box depths by season 525 +- 162, 1151 +- 146, 368 +- 134 ppm (s1 vs s3: 3.9 sigma); per quarter Q7 2265 +- 305 and Q11 1563 +- 278 vs Q9 -194 +- 242 ppm. This is the over-dispersion both the pipeline (chi2/dof 2.05; quartile 1351 vs 453 ppm) and the re-derivation (chi2/dof 3.0; Y4 254 ppm) flagged.

Same clock in other KBONUS light curves on the channel: KIC 11285496 KBONUS PSF flux 65 +- 16 ppm = 2.7 e/s (4.2 sigma); kic-011285117 (different TPF, 14.6 arcmin from the EB, same channels) 582 +- 94 ppm = 2.0 e/s (6.2 sigma); kic-011285661 108 +- 60 ppm = 2.0 e/s. Additive at the ~2 e/s level regardless of source brightness, i.e. ~1.4e-5 of the ~1.4e5 e/s the EB loses in eclipse.

Leak is in KBONUS processing, not the pixels: official Kepler SAP/PDCSAP of KIC 11285496 at the EB ephemeris -14 +- 13 / -7 +- 10 ppm (-0.6 / -0.3 e/s) while its KBONUS flux shows +65 +- 16 ppm; the target's own raw TPF pixels (r < 1.5 px, per-event errors) give 0.48 +- 0.20 e/s overall and -0.06 +- 0.45 e/s in season 1 where 1.8 e/s is expected for a target-hosted dip (4 sigma short).
No physical association: the EB's Gaia DR3 parallax is 1.865 +- 0.017 mas (536 pc) vs 2.86 kpc for the target.
surviving_strengths: The dip is genuinely present in the KBONUS PSF light curve and was recovered blind by the re-derivation (BLS SDE 19.3, SNR ~7); the detection itself is not noise, it is a real signal of instrumental origin.
Odd/even (0.6-1.35 sigma) and Lomb-Scargle (0.7155 d, 88 ppm; nothing at P, P/2, 2P, P/3) are null, as expected for a copied eclipse that repeats identically every 10.79 d.
Gap/quarter-edge timing is not the cause: only 2 of 94 events lie within 0.5 d of a gap; removing the three strongest events leaves 576 ppm.
The target itself is in no KOI, DR25 TCE, Kepler EB, confirmed-planet table or SIMBAD; it is not a previously catalogued object (the EB is).
Pipeline and re-derivation agree with each other on P, depth and event count; the disagreement with reality is entirely the host identification, which the 3-arcmin ephemeris cone could not resolve.
checks_run: Read evidence pack: vet.json, events.csv, fold_events.png, pixel.json (14 quarters), diffimages.png, triage_all.csv (real vs inverted), target metadata, prereg_poolA.json thresholds.

Ephemeris/position match of our P, t0 against KOI cumulative, DR25 TCE, Kirk+2016 Kepler EB and confirmed-planet tables at harmonics 1/4..4 with phase offsets (redteam/ephem_match.py): found K07431.01 / KIC 11285625 at P/2, phase 0.004, 5.63 arcmin.
Kepler EB catalogue lookup for KIC 11285625: P = 10.790444 d, BJD0 142.33451 BKJD, morph 0.23.

Downloaded and folded the official Kepler SAP of KIC 11285625 (15 quarters) at the EB ephemeris: primary 0.1251, secondary 0.0869 at phase 0.4995, width 6.8 h (redteam/eb_lc.py, eb_template.py; profile in eb_profile.csv).
Fitted the EB's eclipse profile (primary and secondary templates) to the target's masked-detrended KBONUS PSF flux with random-phase empirical errors, overall and per season.

TPF header geometry for KIC 11285496 (14 cached quarters) and KIC 11285625 (Q1-Q4): CHANNEL/MODULE/OUTPUT per season and CCD column/row of target, neighbour and EB via WCS (redteam/geometry.py, eb_tpf.py, tpf_headers.py).

Light-curve battery on PSF and SAP flux (redteam/lc_battery.py): T14-box depth with random-phase noise, per-quarter and per-season depths, trapezoid T23/T14 chi2 grid with cadence integration, secondary scan at all phases, odd/even, Lomb-Scargle (detrended and raw, both polarities are equivalent for LS), event timing vs gaps/quarter edges, strongest-event removal, SAP vs PSF absolute deficit.

Pixel-level tests on the raw cached TPFs: per-pixel event-differenced deficit maps with uniform / Gaussian-at-target / scaled-image model comparison (redteam/pixel_bkg.py), and per-event aperture deficits (target r<1.5 px, far pixels, neighbour core, whole stamp, FLUX_BKG) at both the EB primary and secondary phases with honest event-scatter errors (redteam/pixel_events.py).

Folded other KBONUS-BKG light curves at the EB ephemeris: kic-011285496 (downloaded), kic-011285117, kic-011285855, kic-011285661 (redteam/neighbours_fold.py); checked channels of their host TPFs KIC 11285120 and KIC 11285862.
Downloaded and folded the official Kepler SAP and PDCSAP of KIC 11285496 at the EB ephemeris (redteam/official_sap.py).
Gaia DR3 cone search (30 arcsec) and astrophysical_parameters for target and neighbour; Gaia parallax of the EB; SIMBAD 40-arcsec cone and object lookups (redteam/gaia_simbad.py).
Host-parameter consistency: GSP-Phot distance (1948 pc) vs parallax distance (2858 pc), implied luminosity/radius and consequences for Rp and t14_max.
Checked docs for Bienias & Szabo 2025 and Moquin BOI-1 lists (hot Jupiters 2.5-4.8 d and 3.37 d; not this signal).
Searched triage_all.csv for other pool stars within 20 arcmin of the EB and for any pool star at harmonics of 10.790444 d.
what_would_settle_it: Nothing can revive this signal: period match 2.6e-5, epoch match 0.6 h, same channel in all seasons, and the EB's clock present in independent KBONUS sources on the channel. The only observation that would reopen it is a clear deficit in the target's own raw pixels at the ephemeris in season 1 (ch 51) matching the 1.8 e/s the KBONUS flux implies; the measured value is -0.06 +- 0.45 e/s.

For the pipeline (recommendations, nothing changed under pipeline/): extend the ephemeris match from a 3-arcmin cone to the whole channel/module with harmonics 1/3..3, |dP/P| < 1e-3 and epoch within one duration, using the Kepler EB-catalogue period for koi_fpflag_ss = 1 objects; for every survivor fold the KBONUS light curves of the TPF host and two or three other same-channel KBONUS sources at the survivor's ephemeris; compare the TPF host's KBONUS flux with its official SAP/PDCSAP at the ephemeris; treat season-dependent depth as a hard flag.

kic-011285117 (stage-1 survivor at 39.89 d) demonstrably carries this EB's 10.79-d clock at 6.2 sigma in its KBONUS flux; its own 39.9-d signal is unrelated in period but that light curve is contaminated and should be re-examined with that in mind.

The targets file's Rstar for this star (0.86 Rsun, GSP-Phot at 1948 pc) is inconsistent with the parallax distance (2858 pc, M_G = 4.56 -> R ~ 1.3-1.6 Rsun with extinction); Rp and t14_max derived from it are underestimates. Moot for this kill, but relevant for other kpc-distance pool stars.
